topic: Neutron stars: density, spin speed, tiny mountains, gold from collisions
hook: A teaspoon of neutron star weighs a billion tons
tag_reason: NASA is the source of the teaspoon-weighs-a-billion-tons figure
caption:
A single teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth. That is more than every car on the planet put together. These dead stars pack more than the Sun's mass into a city-sized ball.

Part 2 drops tomorrow: magnetars, the strongest magnets in the universe. Follow so the next weird fact finds you. Source: NASA.

1/4 A teaspoon of neutron star weighs a billion tons
Neutron stars squeeze more than our Sun's mass into a ball only about 20 km wide.
📷 Credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/Southampton/W. Ho et al.; Illustration: NASA/CXC/M.Weiss (Public domain) via wikimedia

2/4 They spin insanely fast (716/s)
The fastest one known turns 716 times every second, faster than a kitchen blender.
📷 NASA/MSFC (public domain (NASA)) via nasa

3/4 Mountains under 1 mm (<1 mm)
Their gravity is so extreme that the tallest bumps on the crust are likely less than a millimeter high.
📷 NASA/GSFC (public domain (NASA)) via nasa

4/4 Crashes that forge gold (2017)
In 2017, telescopes watched two neutron stars collide and create heavy elements like gold and platinum.
📷 University of Warwick/Mark Garlick (CC BY 4.0) via wikimedia
